RECIPES.name: Hammer
RECIPES.desc: Unlocks building (B).

RECIPES.name: Rope
RECIPES.desc: Twisted from tall grass.

RECIPES.name: Stone axe
RECIPES.desc: Chop trees twice as fast.

RECIPES.name: Berry basket
RECIPES.desc: An extra berry from every bush.

RECIPES.name: Pickaxe
RECIPES.desc: Break rock and dig iron veins.

RECIPES.name: Ash spear
RECIPES.desc: Longer reach, hits guardians hard.

RECIPES.name: Lightning-bug jar
RECIPES.desc: Eat the honey, scrape the jar, punch the lid. After dark, E by a firefly to catch it: the jar lights your way.

RECIPES.name: Paper kite
RECIPES.desc: Press G to fly it on the west wind. Crows keep away from the garden while it is up.

RECIPES.name: Willow fishing pole
RECIPES.desc: Face the water from the bank and click to cast.

RECIPES.name: Hunting bow
RECIPES.desc: A hickory bow and a quiver of paper-fletched arrows. Hold the mouse button to draw, pan the camera to put the reticle on a deer (it turns gold), and let go. Walk up to it for venison and a hide.

RECIPES.name: Leather boots
RECIPES.desc: Stout tanned-leather boots: sprinting tires you a third less.

RECIPES.name: Sheepskin coat
RECIPES.desc: Take a third less harm.

RECIPES.name: Toadstool stew
RECIPES.desc: Eat (F): heals 40.

RECIPES.name: Skillet cornbread
RECIPES.desc: Eat (F): heals 30.

RECIPES.name: Farmhouse loaf
RECIPES.desc: Eat (F): heals 35. Wheat from the stooks, an egg to glaze it.

RECIPES.name: Buttermilk biscuits
RECIPES.desc: Eat (F): heals 35.

RECIPES.name: Flapjacks
RECIPES.desc: Eat (F): heals 40, well fed.

RECIPES.name: Apple crisp
RECIPES.desc: Eat (F): heals 45, well fed.

RECIPES.name: Pumpkin pie
RECIPES.desc: Eat (F): heals 50, well fed.

RECIPES.name: Venison roast
RECIPES.desc: Eat (F): heals 50, well fed. Venison from the deer you hunt.

RECIPES.name: Pan-fried fish
RECIPES.desc: Eat (F): heals 35.

RECIPES.name: Maple johnnycakes
RECIPES.desc: Eat (F): heals 40, and a sugar rush fills your stamina. Syrup from your sugar shack.

RECIPES.name: Apple pie
RECIPES.desc: Eat (F): heals 55, well fed. Flour from your mill.

RECIPES.name: Honey cake
RECIPES.desc: Eat (F): heals 60, well fed.

RECIPES.name: Smelt iron
RECIPES.desc: Iron for better tools.

RECIPES.name: Iron axe
RECIPES.desc: Fells trees in a stroke or two.

RECIPES.name: Smelt steel
RECIPES.desc: Iron folded with charcoal: hard, bright and true.

RECIPES.name: Steel axe
RECIPES.desc: The best axe in the county: fells any tree in a stroke.

RECIPES.name: Steel pickaxe
RECIPES.desc: Bites through rock and ore like cheese.

RECIPES.name: Iron pickaxe
RECIPES.desc: Splits rock and veins fast.

RECIPES.name: Pie table
RECIPES.desc: "Mrs. Abernathy has entered again. Let's see about that."

RECIPES.name: Best loaf
RECIPES.desc: "A good crust, a good crumb. Your grandmother would approve."

RECIPES.name: Honey & preserves
RECIPES.desc: "Clear as a church window. Clover, is it?"

RECIPES.name: Finest fleece
RECIPES.desc: "Soft as a cloud and not a burr in it."

RECIPES.name: Biggest pumpkins
RECIPES.desc: "We'll need the scales from the feed store for these."

RECIPES.name: Giant pumpkin
RECIPES.desc: "Fetch the scales from the feed store! And a wagon. And another wagon." Two ribbons.

RECIPES.name: Fish story
RECIPES.desc: "Bring OLD WHISKERS himself and I'll believe it. Two ribbons, then."

RECIPES.name: Coil of rope
RECIPES.desc: "Good dry timber! Two coils for it."

RECIPES.name: Jar of honey
RECIPES.desc: "Fresh fish for the road? A jar of honey, then."

RECIPES.name: Sack of ore
RECIPES.desc: "Garden truck for the city folk; ore for you."

RECIPES.name: Load of bricks
RECIPES.desc: "Kiln-fired? The bank in town is putting up a new front."

RECIPES.name: Roll of leather
RECIPES.desc: "Oak-tanned! The harness-maker will want every scrap."

RECIPES.name: Jug of maple syrup
RECIPES.desc: "Real maple, not that cane-sugar slop! Folks in the city go wild for it."

RECIPES.name: Sack of flour
RECIPES.desc: "Stone-ground! The baker in town will pay through the nose."

RECIPES.name: Flour for the mill
RECIPES.desc: "Good hard wheat! The miller owes me one."

RECIPES.name: Old sheepskin
RECIPES.desc: "Clay and stone for my mending. Take this fleece."

RECIPES.name: Honey and rope
RECIPES.desc: "Prime fleece! The ladies in town will knit it up."

RECIPES.name: Grind every edge
RECIPES.desc: The smith puts your axe, pick and spear to his wheel. Sharp as new.

RECIPES.name: Pickaxe
RECIPES.desc: A plain miner's pick, ready-made.

RECIPES.name: Iron axe
RECIPES.desc: Forged while you wait. Fells trees in a stroke or two.

RECIPES.name: Iron pickaxe
RECIPES.desc: Splits rock and veins fast, and bites the silver.

RECIPES.name: Steel axe
RECIPES.desc: His best work. Fells any tree in a stroke.

RECIPES.name: Steel pickaxe
RECIPES.desc: Bites through rock and ore like cheese.

RECIPES.name: Coil of rope
RECIPES.desc: Good hemp, two coils.

RECIPES.name: Sack of apples
RECIPES.desc: Winesaps from back East, a little bruised.

RECIPES.name: Loaf of bread
RECIPES.desc: Baked this morning, still warm.

RECIPES.name: Sack of flour
RECIPES.desc: Two sacks of good white flour.

RECIPES.name: Six-shooter
RECIPES.desc: A single-action revolver and two boxes of cartridges. Hold the mouse button to raise it, put the bead on your mark, let go to fire. Six in the cylinder; then it takes a moment to reload.

RECIPES.name: Buffalo rifle
RECIPES.desc: A heavy single-shot rifle that carries across a valley. Hold to raise it and let it settle, let go to fire; one shot, then reload. It drops a man or a buck at a blow.

RECIPES.name: Box of cartridges
RECIPES.desc: A dozen brass cartridges, for the six-shooter and the rifle both.

RECIPES.name: Beaded moccasins
RECIPES.desc: Soft, quilled and beaded: sprinting tires you a third less (as good as boots).

RECIPES.name: Braided rawhide
RECIPES.desc: A cut of venison for three coils of strong rawhide.

RECIPES.name: Tanned hides
RECIPES.desc: A bar of iron for arrowheads and awls: two good hides in return.

RECIPES.name: Medicine root
RECIPES.desc: The elder trades a dried root of wild sang for a jar of honey.

RECIPES.name: Ship lumber
RECIPES.desc: "A carload of good timber for the Denver yards: six dollars on the bill of lading."

RECIPES.name: Ship dressed stone
RECIPES.desc: "Foundation stone for the new courthouse at Cheyenne. Four dollars."

RECIPES.name: Ship bricks
RECIPES.desc: "Kiln-fired brick, packed in straw. Seven dollars the lot."

RECIPES.name: Ship corn
RECIPES.desc: "Sacked corn for the Kansas City mills: five dollars."

RECIPES.name: Ship pumpkins
RECIPES.desc: "Crated pumpkins for the Chicago markets, five dollars."

RECIPES.name: Ship apples
RECIPES.desc: "A barrel of apples, packed in sawdust: four dollars."

RECIPES.name: Ship wool
RECIPES.desc: "Baled fleece for the Lowell mills. Six dollars."

RECIPES.name: Ship hides
RECIPES.desc: "Two good hides for a St. Louis furrier: seven dollars."

RECIPES.name: Ship honey
RECIPES.desc: "Crocks of clover honey for a confectioner back East, seven dollars."

RECIPES.name: Ship flour
RECIPES.desc: "Your own milling, in sacks: six dollars."

RECIPES.name: Ship maple syrup
RECIPES.desc: "A San Francisco hotel will take all the syrup you can send. Eight dollars for two jugs."

RECIPES.name: Ship leather
RECIPES.desc: "Tanned leather for a Kansas City saddler: nine dollars."

RECIPES.name: Jugs of maple syrup
RECIPES.desc: "Boiled down in the sugar bush up the hollow. Two jugs, three dollars."

RECIPES.name: A cord of birch
RECIPES.desc: "Split and seasoned. The woodcutters bring in more than we can burn."

RECIPES.name: Bread for the woodcutters
RECIPES.desc: "Beans and bacon, beans and bacon. Two real loaves and they’d pay anything."

RECIPES.name: File a mining claim
RECIPES.desc: The keeper is the district recorder too. Twenty-five dollars files the ground back along the line: an old adit with a gold vein in it, a windlass and a cart. Work it once a day (E at the adit, with a pickaxe).

RECIPES.name: Hire a hand for your claim
RECIPES.desc: A steady old Cornish miner, out of work since the Comstock. He pitches his tent on your claim and works the vein every day; his takings wait for you in the ore cart.

RECIPES.name: A stamp mill for your claim
RECIPES.desc: A little five-stamp mill, freighted up from Denver and put up beside your adit. It crushes the quartz fine, so far more of the gold comes out: your hand brings in two more pinches a day, you one more.

RECIPES.name: Sacks of ore
RECIPES.desc: "Tailings from the silver diggings, rich in iron. Three sacks."

RECIPES.name: A bar of steel
RECIPES.desc: "Drill steel from the mine’s smithy. Hard as the hills."

RECIPES.name: A pie for the diggings
RECIPES.desc: "A whole pie! The boys at the diggings haven’t seen one since Easter."

RECIPES.name: A string of fish
RECIPES.desc: "Catfish and pickerel, caught this morning off the skiffs."

RECIPES.name: Medicine root
RECIPES.desc: "Wild sang, dug on the hummocks where the mist lies thickest."

RECIPES.name: Rope for the skiffs
RECIPES.desc: "Everything out here is poled or tied. Three coils, five dollars."

RECIPES.name: Sheaves of wheat
RECIPES.desc: "Hard red wheat, as far as you can see. Five sheaves, two dollars."

RECIPES.name: Tanned buffalo leather
RECIPES.desc: "Tanned on the prairie, thick and soft. Two hides."

RECIPES.name: Iron for plow points
RECIPES.desc: "The sod breaks a plow point a week. A bar of iron, six dollars."

RECIPES.name: Winter pelts
RECIPES.desc: "Prime winter fur from the trappers’ lines. Two pelts."

RECIPES.name: Pine charcoal
RECIPES.desc: "Burned in the high kilns. Three sacks, for your steel."

RECIPES.name: Flour for the lumber camp
RECIPES.desc: "The camp cook is down to the sweepings. Two sacks, seven dollars."

RECIPES.name: Storehouse casks
RECIPES.desc: A wagonload of oak casks and barrels for your storehouse: it holds 45 of each thing from the works instead of 30.

RECIPES.name: Rain barrel and pail
RECIPES.desc: A water butt under the eaves and a cedar pail: your crops and garden grow a quarter faster.

RECIPES.name: Sell him wood
RECIPES.desc: "Straight-grained oak or ash makes good staves. Three dollars for six."

RECIPES.name: Sheepskin coat
RECIPES.desc: Ready-made, fleece-lined, off the rack. Take a third less harm, and keep warm of a cold night.

RECIPES.name: Leather boots
RECIPES.desc: Stout boots from a Boston cobbler: sprinting tires you a third less.

RECIPES.name: Berry basket
RECIPES.desc: A split-oak basket: an extra berry from every bush.

RECIPES.name: Lightning-bug jar
RECIPES.desc: A Mason jar with a punched tin lid, for catching fireflies after dark.

RECIPES.name: Bolt of calico
RECIPES.desc: Calico and twine by the yard: four fibre for your crafting.

RECIPES.name: Sell her a hide
RECIPES.desc: "A good hide makes a good coat. Three dollars."

RECIPES.name: Sack of laying mash
RECIPES.desc: Five mornings' worth. Scatter a scoop in the coop each morning and the hens lay two more eggs.

RECIPES.name: Sack of oats
RECIPES.desc: Rolled oats for your horse: three feeds. A morning feed (automatic, when you first ride that day) and she runs a quarter faster all day.

RECIPES.name: Sell him corn
RECIPES.desc: "Four good ears. Three dollars, and I'll shell it myself."

RECIPES.name: Sell him wool
RECIPES.desc: "Three fleeces, clean? Five dollars. The mill down the valley pays me back."

RECIPES.name: Deposit $10
RECIPES.desc: Into the iron safe, written in the ledger in a copperplate hand.

RECIPES.name: Deposit $50
RECIPES.desc: "A tidy sum. It will grow, sir, slow and sure as an oak."

RECIPES.name: Withdraw $10
RECIPES.desc: Counted out onto the counter in clean bills.

RECIPES.name: Withdraw $50
RECIPES.desc: "Spend it wisely, sir. Or at least spend it in town."

RECIPES.name: Pumpkin pie
RECIPES.desc: Still warm from the oven, with a lattice top. (For the fair table too, if you're not proud.)

RECIPES.name: Apple pie
RECIPES.desc: Winesaps and cinnamon under a crimped crust.

RECIPES.name: Honey cake
RECIPES.desc: A dense little cake glazed with clover honey.

RECIPES.name: Pan of biscuits
RECIPES.desc: Buttermilk biscuits, a dozen to the pan.

RECIPES.name: Sell her flour
RECIPES.desc: "Two sacks from your own mill? I'll give you five dollars and be glad of it."

RECIPES.name: Sell her eggs
RECIPES.desc: "Half a dozen good brown eggs: four dollars."

RECIPES.name: Sell her a pumpkin
RECIPES.desc: "For the pies. Three dollars, and a slice when it's baked."

RECIPES.name: Jar of honey
RECIPES.desc: Clover honey, sealed with wax.

RECIPES.name: Side of leather
RECIPES.desc: Oak-tanned, from the tannery downriver.

RECIPES.name: Bar of iron
RECIPES.desc: Pig iron, freighted up from the railhead.

RECIPES.name: Bar of steel
RECIPES.desc: Pittsburgh steel. Dear, but it holds an edge.

RECIPES.name: Silver ore
RECIPES.desc: "Silver, by thunder! Out of the Redrock Breaks? Steel and iron for it, and no questions."

RECIPES.name: Fen pearls
RECIPES.desc: "River pearls! The jeweller in town will weep. Mind you, so did the Hodag."

RECIPES.name: Wild sang root
RECIPES.desc: "Ginseng! Dug from the Hollows? The druggist pays its weight in coin."

RECIPES.name: Amber
RECIPES.desc: "Pine amber, with a gnat in it! The lamp-maker will take all you bring."

RECIPES.name: Thunder egg
RECIPES.desc: "Crack one open on the prairie, did you? Purple as a bishop. I'll have it."

RECIPES.name: Pig iron
RECIPES.desc: "Fine pelts! Two bars of pig iron for them."

REQUESTS.name: Two pumpkin pies
REQUESTS.desc: "The widow Hale says she'll marry me if I bring her two of your pies."

REQUESTS.name: Half a dozen eggs
REQUESTS.desc: "Six good brown eggs for the cook at the mill, and I'll make it worth your while."

REQUESTS.name: Five fleeces of wool
REQUESTS.desc: "The ladies of the quilting circle are fresh out of wool. Five, if you can spare them?"

REQUESTS.name: Two plates of fried fish
REQUESTS.desc: "I haven't had a hot supper since Tuesday. Two plates of your fried fish?"

REQUESTS.name: A bushel of apples
REQUESTS.desc: "Ten good apples for the cider press in town. I'll pay in honey."

REQUESTS.name: Corn and pumpkins for the fair
REQUESTS.desc: "The county fair's coming. Eight ears of corn and two pumpkins to show off?"

REQUESTS.name: Three buttermilk biscuits
REQUESTS.desc: "Three of your biscuits, for the long road west."
